common.footerBody: Core setup is accountless. SafeWeb does not provide browsing history, child profiles, a safety score, or unrestricted DNS administration.

home.title: Set up safer DNS without creating an account
home.summary: SafeWeb guides a parent through phone safeguards and encrypted DNS, then keeps protection claims tied to current evidence.

cards.title: Accountless core
cards.body: Start, understand, troubleshoot, remove, and recover without signing in.

cards.title: Truthful status
cards.body: A saved setting or account never becomes technical verification by itself.

cards.title: Small scope
cards.body: No browsing history, child account, activity timeline, or broad DNS console.

home.noteBody: Each protection layer is reported separately. Unsupported or uncertain conditions stop with a clear next action instead of a positive claim.

howItWorks.title: Phone, Internet, then relevant services
howItWorks.summary: SafeWeb separates each layer so one successful step never certifies another.

cards.title: 1. Phone
cards.body: Review the supported native safeguard. Parent confirmation is recorded only as confirmation.

cards.title: 2. Internet
cards.body: Configure the approved encrypted DNS path and verify it with qualifying technical evidence.

cards.title: 3. Services
cards.body: Show only a currently approved relevant service safeguard; zero applicable services is valid.

howItWorks.noteBody: The Protection Map keeps verified, confirmed, action-needed, uncertain, not-covered, and removed states distinct.

compatibility.title: Use only a supported setup path
compatibility.summary: SafeWeb currently guides supported Android Private DNS and the approved iPhone encrypted-DNS profile route.

cards.title: Android
cards.body: Supported Android phones use the Private DNS provider-hostname control where it is available and usable.

cards.title: iPhone
cards.body: Supported iPhones use the approved encrypted-DNS profile flow with explicit iOS installation approval.

cards.title: Managed or conflicting devices
cards.body: If device policy, VPN, Private Relay, another resolver, or an unsupported platform blocks a reliable result, SafeWeb reports the limitation instead of inventing a workaround.

compatibility.noteBody: Do not weaken employer, school, or security controls merely to make SafeWeb show a positive state.

limits.title: Protection is evidence-bounded
limits.summary: SafeWeb can reduce exposure through supported safeguards, but it cannot prove complete device or child safety.

cards.title: Verified
cards.body: Reserved for current qualifying technical evidence for that layer.

cards.title: Status uncertain
cards.body: Used when current evidence is incomplete or conflicting.

cards.title: Not covered
cards.body: Used when the current platform, network, or service path is outside supported scope.

limits.noteBody: Removing SafeWeb DNS, deleting a future account record, logging out, and deleting anonymous web state are different operations.

privacy.title: Minimise data by design
privacy.summary: The accountless public/start experience does not need identity, browsing history, activity history, or raw DNS history.

cards.title: No identity required
cards.body: The core setup path remains usable without a parent or child account.

cards.title: No surveillance view
cards.body: There is no history timeline, top-sites list, child profile, or raw query dashboard.

cards.title: Separate domains
cards.body: Any future optional account/device records remain separate from anonymous setup state unless an explicit approved transfer is later implemented.

privacy.noteTitle: This is a product privacy boundary
privacy.noteBody: Public legal or regulatory conclusions remain outside this implementation and are not inferred from this page.

help.title: Solve the specific issue in front of you
help.summary: SafeWeb support starts from the current setup or verification problem and avoids broad data collection.

cards.title: Setup or verification
cards.body: Check the relevant platform setting and only retry after a condition changes or new evidence exists.

cards.title: Blocked site or service
cards.body: A content problem does not automatically change the DNS-path evidence state.

cards.title: Removal and recovery
cards.body: Remove only the SafeWeb-owned setting or profile, then confirm ordinary connectivity without claiming protection remains active.

help.noteBody: Routine help should not request browsing history, raw DNS logs, child profile data, passwords, tokens, or broad network dumps.

status.title: Status must stay separate from protection state
status.summary: A service or provider incident can affect availability, but operational availability never proves that a device is protected.

cards.title: Current publication boundary
cards.body: This baseline does not publish or claim live production status. A later approved status surface must use aggregate or synthetic operational evidence.

status.noteBody: The existence of this route is not evidence of production activation, deployment, launch, or current service availability.

start.title: Start without signing in
start.summary: Choose the phone you are setting up. The current baseline uses URL routing only and stores no journey state.

cards.title: What happens next
cards.body: SafeWeb routes to the supported native phone safeguard, then the approved DNS setup instructions.

cards.title: What does not happen
cards.body: Starting setup does not create an account, identify a child, or record browsing activity.

start.noteBody: Optional account continuity belongs to a later bounded feature slice and cannot become a prerequisite for core value.

route.title: Which phone are you setting up?
route.summary: Choose the current supported path. SafeWeb selects the approved DNS mechanism; you do not need to choose a DNS protocol.
route.noteBody: If the needed control is absent, locked, managed, or incompatible, use compatibility guidance instead of a speculative setup.

native.androidTitle: Review the current Android family safeguard
native.iphoneTitle: Review Screen Time / Content & Privacy Restrictions
native.androidBody: Review the supported Android native safeguard for this phone. SafeWeb does not silently change platform controls.
native.iphoneBody: Review the supported Apple Screen Time / Content & Privacy Restrictions setting. SafeWeb does not silently change platform controls.
native.noteBody: Your confirmation can record that you completed this step, but it never becomes technical DNS verification.

dns.androidIntro: Open Android's Private DNS setting and choose the provider-hostname option. Enter dns.usesafeweb.com and save. Use the hostname exactly as shown — not an https:// address. Return to SafeWeb so protection can be checked.
androidSteps: Save the setting and return to SafeWeb.
dns.iphoneTitle: Install the approved SafeWeb DNS profile on iPhone
dns.iphoneIntro: Get the exact verified SafeWeb DNS profile for this environment, then follow iPhone's profile-installation flow and explicitly approve the installation in iOS. SafeWeb does not install it silently.
dns.noteBody: A saved setting, installed profile, or signed-in account cannot become Verified without the separately approved technical verification check.
